intervals.label: full array proposed
intervals.note: Start is the submission date of the 2020 Nature Astronomy design paper; the collaboration's own official site still described the full multi-cubic-kilometre array as 'proposed' when re-checked on 2026-09-18. This interval alone would leave the experiment status 'proposed'; the pathfinder programme, which was deployed and took data until it was recovered in July 2023, is recorded in the STRAW interval below.
intervals.quote: The Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment (P-ONE) is a proposed large-volume neutrino telescope in the Northeast Pacific Ocean, off the coast of Vancouver Island, Canada.

end.display: recovered in the summer 2023 ONC expedition (item dated 24 August 2023 says 'last month')

intervals.label: STRAW pathfinder programme (deployed and taking data until recovered in July 2023)
intervals.note: The STRAW pathfinder (detector:p-one) took data at Cascadia Basin from January 2019 until its three moorings were recovered in the summer 2023 ONC expedition (P-ONE news quoting Ocean Networks Canada, 24 August 2023; quote above). Status 'commissioning' reflects the production array still being readied: the official site (checked 2026-09-18) says P-ONE-1, its first production detection line, has completed integration and a wet test on land and in harbour, but 'will be deployed' to depth in 2026.
intervals.quote: The three moorings (a 500-metre string and two 150 metre in length) were disconnected and recovered during last month’s summer 2023 #ONCAbyss expedition

intervals.label: P-ONE-1 first full-scale line and demonstrator construction (line integrated, awaiting deployment)
intervals.note: The official P-ONE news page (checked 2026-10-25) lists as its newest items the wet test of 23 June 2026 and the integration of P-ONE-1 (assembled and integrated 28 April 2026); it reports no deployment, and no other source reporting a deployment was found, so the first line is recorded as awaiting deployment (a plan to deploy by the end of August 2026 is recorded as a planned phase). The STRAW pathfinder moorings (a 500 m string and two 150 m strings) were recovered in the summer 2023 ONC expedition (July 2023; ONC item of 24 August 2023), so nothing of P-ONE has been operating undersea since then. The next stage, the P-ONE Demonstrator (up to six detector lines), is in procurement of long-lead components, with final assembly at TRIUMF 'between 2027 and 2028' (a plan). The start year is a lower bound inferred from 'nearly three years' to April 2026; the news item gives no construction start date.
intervals.quote: the 1 km-long detector line P-ONE-1 was fully assembled and integrated (Figure 1), representing the culmination of nearly three years of coordinated international development and engineering efforts

start.display: 'nearly three years' of development before April 2026

intervals.label: P-ONE-1 assembled and integrated at TRIUMF
intervals.quote: On April 28, the 1 km-long detector line P-ONE-1 was fully assembled and integrated

intervals.label: P-ONE-1 final shallow-water wet test (Granville Island, Vancouver)
intervals.quote: On June 23, 2026, the P-ONE Collaboration and its global partners reached yet another major milestone: The first full-scale detector line of P-ONE, P-ONE-1, successfully completed its final pre-deployment shallow-water test

intervals.label: P-ONE-1 deployment at Cascadia Basin (planned)
intervals.note: A plan, not a report: "the collaboration aims to deploy P-ONE-1, including the full acoustic calibration infrastructure on the seafloor, by the end of August 2026. Detector commissioning and initial data-taking activities will commence immediately following deployment." The deployment campaign also includes a new 30-km subsea cable extension. No source dated after 23 June 2026 reports the deployment (the P-ONE news page has nothing newer), so the experiment stays in `construction`; if the line is in the water the state would be `commissioning`. Re-check before release.
intervals.quote: the collaboration aims to deploy P-ONE-1, including the full acoustic calibration infrastructure on the seafloor, by the end of August 2026

quantity.quote: An established ONC site, known as the Cascadia Basin (fig. 1), 2,660 m below sea level, provides an ideal environment for a large scale undersea neutrino telescope.

name: P-ONE
notes: detector:p-one is placed at site:cascadia-basin-p-one, whose coordinates (47°46'N, 127°46'W, to 1 arcminute) are the position the STRAW pathfinder paper (arXiv:1810.13265) gives for the ONC deep-sea infrastructure at the Cascadia Basin site (depth 2660 m per the EPJC site-characterization paper; 'Cascadia Basin, ~200 km off the coast of British Columbia/Vancouver Island, Canada'). It is the position of the cabled site (approximate), not a surveyed seafloor deployment position.

Timeline per the collaboration's own pages/papers: STRAW pathfinder deployed Spring 2018, commissioning completed January 2019; STRAW-b under construction as of the 2021 paper with deployment then planned for 2020 (i.e. the 2021 paper's schedule predates its own writing, an internal inconsistency in that source, left unresolved); P-ONE Explorer deployment was planned for 2023-2024 in the 2020 design paper; the official site (re-fetched 2026-09-18) states 'In 2026, the first detection line of P-ONE will be deployed' (future tense) and separately lists completed milestones 'Successful wet test of P-ONE-1 in Vancouver's Granville Island' and 'Completed integration of first detector line P-ONE-1' -- read together, P-ONE-1 has been built and tested on land/in harbour but the site's own present-tense wording indicates it has not yet been deployed to depth at Cascadia Basin.

physics_goals.value: Build a multi-cubic-kilometre neutrino telescope in the deep Pacific Ocean to detect high-energy astrophysical neutrinos

summary.plain: A planned neutrino telescope for the deep Pacific Ocean off Canada's west coast, building on an undersea science network. A small pathfinder instrument has been actively taking data there since 2019, proving the technology, while the full telescope and its first production line are still being built.
summary.technical: Multi-cubic-kilometre water-Cherenkov neutrino telescope proposed for the Cascadia Basin (2660 m depth) on Ocean Networks Canada's NEPTUNE cabled infrastructure off Vancouver Island. The STRAW pathfinder (deployed Spring 2018) has been actively taking data since January 2019, validating deep-sea deployment and optical-background characterization; P-ONE-1, the planned first production detection line, has completed integration and a wet test but had not yet been deployed to depth as of the 2026-09-18 re-check. The full design array remains at the proposal stage.
